Write a self-describing CSV

Source: R/io_write.R
cs_write.Rd

One-call writer. Builds a schema from df (unless one is supplied), packetizes it, sizes and stripes the redundancy, appends the _schema (and, by default, _canary) columns, and writes the CSV. When sidecar is not FALSE, also writes a Frictionless datapackage.json beside it with the file hash.

Usage

cs_write(
  df,
  path,
  schema = NULL,
  sidecar = TRUE,
  mtu = CS_DEFAULT_MTU,
  f = CS_DEFAULT_F,
  eps = CS_DEFAULT_EPS,
  c = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  canary = TRUE,
  k = CS_DEFAULT_CANARY_K,
  writer = "auto",
  verbose = TRUE
)

cs_write_csv(out, path, writer = "auto")

Arguments

df

A data frame.

path

Output CSV path.

schema

An cs_schema; built from df if NULL.

sidecar

TRUE to write datapackage.json beside the CSV, FALSE for none, or a path.

mtu

Maximum packet length in characters.

f

Fraction of rows the redundancy is designed to survive.

eps

Acceptable packet-loss probability.

c, p

Override the chosen number of schema columns / packets per cell.

canary

Whether to add the _canary column.

k

Canary samples per variable.

writer

CSV writer backend: "auto", "readr", or "base".

verbose

Print the layout summary.

out

A fully-assembled character data frame (data plus meta columns).

Value

The cs_schema, invisibly, with a layout attribute.

Examples

tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
cs_write(data.frame(id = 1:5, g = factor(c("a", "b", "a", "b", "a"))),
         tmp, sidecar = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
